How to use this book

What the book covers, what each box does, who the case companies are, and how this site works with no internet connection.

This book covers every Learning Outcome Statement in CMA Part 1, Section C (Strategy and Budgeting), effective September 1, 2024. It is written in graded English (B1+ to B2) with the exact exam terms, and it bridges each term to Arabic.

From the September/October 2026 testing window, English-language CMA exams have 100 multiple-choice questions followed by two case-based questions (CBQs). The Learning Outcome Statements did not change. Every chapter therefore ends with multiple-choice practice and a case-style set in the CBQ format.

Three parts. Part I, Chapters 1 to 5, covers strategy and budgeting foundations. Part II, Chapters 6 to 10, covers the master budget. Part III, Chapters 11 to 18, covers measuring and managing performance.

Each chapter follows the same pattern: an opener figure, learning objectives with LOS codes, key terms, numbered sections, a section check after each section, a chapter summary figure, practice questions, a case question in the official exam format and full answers with explanations.

The case companies

■ U.S. GAAP

Orontes Foods, Inc.

A food and beverage producer based in Amman, Jordan, listed in the United States, so it reports under U.S. GAAP. It makes olive oil and tahini in Amman and frozen pastries in Dubai. Worked through 13 of this book's chapters.

■ U.S. GAAP

Barada Wholesale, Inc.

A small U.S. GAAP distributor in Amman and one of Orontes's largest customers, used for the case-style sets at the end of each chapter. Worked through 2 of this book's chapters.

Numbers

Amounts are in whole U.S. dollars unless a table says USD 000, as each one's heading says. Examples that begin with “Suppose” are illustrative: they are not part of a case company's reported statements. Figure and question numbers keep their chapter prefix, for example F311-03.

Where the exam asks you to type an amount, enter it without the $ sign and without commas — for example 1250. The numeric boxes in this site accept answers the same way.

The boxes inside the Brief

Press Brief at the top of any page and these are the boxes you meet inside it. This volume carries 58 of them.

WORKED EXAMPLE

A calculation or analysis, step by step.

FALSE-FRIEND ALERT

An Arabic or French term that looks right but means something else in U.S. GAAP. Stock is the classic: shares in U.S. English, inventory in French and British English.

How this site works

  • Every screen asks you to decide something. There are no screens that only show you a figure or a statement: the author's figures appear inside the exercise built on them, where you need them, and every screen is marked. This volume has 645 section checks.
  • Press Brief at the top of any page for the explanation. It gives that section in the author's own words, the terms with their Arabic and a speaker for each, one drawing of the mechanism, and a list of what the page asks you to do. It never contains an answer to an exercise on that page.
  • Every exercise has Check Answers and Try Again. Try Again re-shuffles the item and clears your marks — it never reveals the answer as a shortcut.
  • Answers are shuffled every time, and in a matching or sorting exercise there are always more tiles than places to put them, so the last one is never free.
  • Feedback leads with your own choice. When you are wrong, the first thing you read is the reason for the option you picked, taken from the book's own explanations.
  • Every term is bridged to Arabic. Each of the 18 chapters has a term bank that drills its key words both ways, and the glossary and the index of terms gather them all.
  • Drag-and-drop always has a click path. Tap a tile, then tap where it goes. Everything is operable from the keyboard too: Tab to a tile, Enter to pick it up, Tab to a target, Enter to drop.
  • Pronunciation uses your computer's voices. On Windows, Chrome and Microsoft Edge expose the installed voices directly. If an Arabic icon is dimmed, no Arabic voice is installed — Windows: Settings → Time & language → Speech → Add voices → Arabic.
  • Progress is saved in this browser on this computer. Nothing is sent anywhere. The foot of any chapter page has a button to clear it.
  • No web server, no internet, no install. Open index.html straight from the folder. Press ← and → to move between screens, and use your browser's print command for a clean worksheet of any practice page.

The first part of this book

1 · Strategic Planning: Purpose, Mission and Time Frame — six numbered sections and 0 graded exercises, then the summary, the term bank, the practice questions, the case question, a mixed review and the full answer section.

2 · Analysing the Environment and Choosing a Strategy — seven numbered sections and 0 graded exercises, then the summary, the term bank, the practice questions, the case question, a mixed review and the full answer section.

3 · Budgeting Concepts: Roles, People and Behavior — seven numbered sections and 0 graded exercises, then the summary, the term bank, the practice questions, the case question, a mixed review and the full answer section.

4 · Budget Systems I: Master, Project and Activity-Based Budgets — six numbered sections and 0 graded exercises, then the summary, the term bank, the practice questions, the case question, a mixed review and the full answer section.

5 · Budget Systems II: Zero-Based, Rolling and Flexible Budgets — six numbered sections and 0 graded exercises, then the summary, the term bank, the practice questions, the case question, a mixed review and the full answer section.

Chapters 6 to 18 are built too, from The Sales and Production Budgets to Critical Success Factors, KPIs and the Balanced Scorecard. Every chapter follows the same shape. The number of sections is the book's, not a template's — across this volume it runs from 4 to 6. Each chapter saves its progress separately, so resetting one leaves the others alone.
